questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) to safeguard the rights of the Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 338**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 338** of the **Constitution of India** mandates the establishment of the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)**, a **constitutional body** dedicated to protecting the rights of the **Scheduled Castes**.
 
• The commission is entrusted with the duty to investigate and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the **Scheduled Castes** under the **Constitution** or any other laws of the country.
 
• The **89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**, bifurcated the former joint commission into two separate entities: the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes** under **Article 338** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** under **Article 338A**.
 
• The **NCSC** consists of a **Chairperson**, a **Vice-Chairperson**, and **three other members**, all of whom are appointed by the **President of India** by warrant under his hand and seal.
 
• While investigating any matter or inquiry, the commission possesses all the powers of a **Civil Court**, specifically regarding the summoning of witnesses and the production of documents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 340**:

 
 
• Empowers the **President** to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally **backward classes**.
 
• This article formed the basis for the establishment of the **Mandal Commission** in **1979**.
 
 
 
• **Article 330**:
 
 
• Provides for the **reservation of seats** for the **Scheduled Castes** and the **Scheduled Tribes** in the **House of the People** (Lok Sabha).
 
• The number of reserved seats is determined by the proportion of their population in each **State** or **Union Territory**.
 
 
 
• **Article 350**:
 
 
• Relates to the language to be used in representations for the **redress of grievances** to any authority of the **Union** or a **State**.
 
• It is associated with **Article 350B**, which provides for a **Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities**.

questions.question: Who was chosen as the first president of the Indian National Congress (INC) during its first session?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Congress** (INC) held its inaugural session from **December 28 to December 31, 1885**, marking the beginning of a structured national movement in India.
 
• **Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee**, a distinguished **Bengali barrister**, was elected as the **first President** of the session, representing the **Moderate** phase of Indian politics.
 
• The venue for this historic meeting was **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College** in **Bombay** (present-day Mumbai).
 
• The session was initially planned to be held in **Poona**, but the location was shifted to Bombay following a sudden outbreak of **cholera** in the city.
 
• The formation of the Congress was facilitated by **Allan Octavian Hume** (A.O. Hume), a retired British official who served as the first **General Secretary**.
 
• A total of **72 delegates** from across India attended the first session, primarily consisting of **lawyers**, **journalists**, and **intellectuals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surendranath Banerjee**:

 
 
• Founded the **Indian National Association** in **1876**, which was a precursor to the INC.
 
• He was absent from the first INC session because he was presiding over the **National Conference** in **Calcutta** at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal**:
 
 
• Recognized as the **'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts'** in India and a key leader of the **Swadeshi Movement**.
 
• He was a member of the **Extremist** group within the Congress, forming the famous **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio with **Lala Lajpat Rai** and **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**.
 
 
 
• **Pherozeshah Mehta**:
 
 
• A prominent **Moderate** leader often referred to as the **'Lion of Bombay'** for his influence in the **Bombay Municipal Corporation**.
 
• He served as the President of the Congress during its **1890 session** held in **Calcutta**.

questions.question: In June 2025, Indian author Banu Mushtaq, in her acclaimed book Heart Lamp, explores which central theme through her vivid portrayal of everyday characters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caste and religious oppression**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heart Lamp** is a celebrated collection of short stories by the veteran **Kannada** writer and activist **Banu Mushtaq**, translated to reach a wider global audience.
 
• The central theme of the book revolves around **Caste and religious oppression**, particularly focusing on the intersectional struggles of **Muslim women** within the socio-political landscape of **Karnataka**.
 
• Mushtaq utilizes a **realist narrative style** to depict how everyday characters navigate the complexities of **communalism**, **patriarchy**, and **social stratification**.
 
• The stories highlight the **marginalization** of minority groups, providing a nuanced perspective on how **religious identity** and **caste hierarchies** dictate access to justice and dignity.
 
• By focusing on **ordinary lives**, the author exposes the structural violence inherent in **communal divisions** while celebrating the quiet resilience of those living on the fringes of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banu Mushtaq**:

 
 
• She is a prominent **feminist voice** in **South Indian literature** and a practicing **advocate** who has dedicated her life to **legal activism** for women.
 
• Her literary works are deeply influenced by her legal background, often addressing issues of **domestic violence**, **family law**, and **civil liberties**.
 
• She has been a recipient of the prestigious **Karnataka Sahitya Academy Award**, recognizing her enduring impact on **Kannada literature**.
 
 
 
• **Context of the Work**:
 
 
• **Heart Lamp** serves as a critical document of the **minority experience** in India, challenging monolithic narratives and providing a space for **subaltern voices**.
 
• The book is significant for its exploration of **secularism** and the **pluralistic fabric** of Indian society during periods of heightened **religious polarization**.

questions.question: Which of the following bodies approved the appointment of S Krishnan as Chairman of J&K Bank?

options.text: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India(IRDAI)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** granted its approval for the appointment of **S Krishnan** as the **Part-time Chairman** of **Jammu and Kashmir Bank (J&K Bank)** in **November 2023**.
 
• This approval was issued in accordance with **Section 10BB** and **Section 35B** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, which grants the **RBI** the authority to regulate the appointment of **Chairmen**, **MDs**, and **CEOs** in scheduled commercial banks.
 
• The **Board of Directors** of **J&K Bank** recommended **S Krishnan** to lead the board, ensuring that the institution maintains high standards of **corporate governance** and **regulatory compliance**.
 
• The tenure for this appointment is set for a period of **three years**, during which **S Krishnan** is expected to oversee the strategic direction of the **Srinagar-headquartered** bank.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India**, as the **central banking institution**, performs this function to safeguard the interests of depositors and ensure the efficient management of banking entities within the **Indian financial system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Profile of S Krishnan:**

 
 
• He previously served as the **Managing Director and CEO** of **Punjab & Sind Bank** from September 2020 to May 2022.
 
• His career includes significant leadership roles such as **Executive Director** at both **Syndicate Bank** and **Canara Bank**, amassing over **38 years** of banking experience.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Bank (J&K Bank):**
 
 
• Incorporated in **1938**, it is a **Scheduled Commercial Bank** where the **Government of Jammu & Kashmir** holds a majority stake.
 
• It operates as the primary financial institution for the **Union Territories** of **Jammu & Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
 
 
 
• **Other Regulatory Bodies:**
 
 
• **IRDAI:** Established in **1999**, the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India** regulates the **insurance** and **re-insurance** industries.
 
• **NITI Aayog:** Replacing the **Planning Commission** in **2015**, it serves as the apex **public policy think tank** of the **Government of India**.
 
• **Ministry of Finance:** A ministry of the **Government of India** concerned with the **economy**, **taxation**, and **financial legislation**.

questions.question: Which of the following dancers is acclaimed for their mastery and teaching of Odissi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kelucharan Mohapatra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kelucharan Mohapatra** was a legendary Indian classical dancer, choreographer, and percussionist who is credited with the **20th-century revival** of **Odissi**, a classical dance form originating from **Odisha**.
 
• He was the first person from the state of **Odisha** to be honored with the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2000**, which is India's second-highest civilian award.
 
• Known for his mastery of **Abhinaya** (expressive acting), he extensively researched ancient temple sculptures, such as those at the **Konark Sun Temple** and **Puri Jagannath Temple**, to reconstruct and systematize **Odissi** movements.
 
• In **1993**, he established **Srjan**, a premier dance institution in **Bhubaneswar**, to pass on his knowledge to future generations, training iconic dancers like **Sonal Mansingh** and **Samyukta Panigrahi**.
 
• Apart from dancing, he was an expert player of the **Pakhawaj**, **Mridangam**, and **Tabla**, integrating deep rhythmic complexity into his choreographic works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitara Devi**:

 
 
• She was an eminent exponent of **Kathak** and was often referred to as the **Kathak Queen**; she received the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **1969** and the **Padma Shri** in **1973**.
 
 
 
• **Vempati Chinna Satyam**:
 
 
• He was a renowned **Kuchipudi** dancer and teacher who founded the **Kuchipudi Art Academy** in **Madras** (now **Chennai**) in **1963** to refine and promote this **Andhra Pradesh** dance form.
 
 
 
• **Kalamandalam Leelamma**:
 
 
• A prominent **Mohiniyattam** dancer from **Kerala**, she was highly regarded for her performances and her academic contributions at the **Kerala Kalamandalam** deemed university.

questions.question: Which of the following British Indian government legislations provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta, comprising one chief justice and three other judges?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act of 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first major step taken by the **British Parliament** to exercise control over the **East India Company’s** administration in **India**.
 
• Section 13 of this legislation specifically authorized the **British Crown** to establish a **Supreme Court of Judicature** at **Fort William** in **Calcutta**.
 
• The Act mandated that the court would consist of a **Chief Justice** and **three other judges** (Puisne Judges) to oversee legal matters involving **British subjects** and those in the service of the Company.
 
• Established in **1774**, the court functioned as a **Court of Record** with wide-ranging civil and criminal jurisdiction; **Sir Elijah Impey** was appointed as the first **Chief Justice**.
 
• The Act also transformed the **Governor of Bengal** into the **Governor-General of Bengal**, with **Warren Hastings** being the first to hold this prestigious post.
 
• It prohibited the employees of the **East India Company** from engaging in any **private trade** or accepting **presents and bribes** from the local population to curb corruption.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pitt’s India Act of 1784**:

 
 
• This Act introduced a **system of double government** by establishing the **Board of Control** to supervise political and military affairs.
 
• It clearly distinguished between the **commercial** and **political functions** of the Company for the first time.
 
 
 
• **Amending Act of 1781**:
 
 
• Known as the **Act of Settlement**, it was passed to rectify the defects and jurisdictional ambiguities of the **Regulating Act of 1773**.
 
• It exempted the **Governor-General and Council** from the jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court** for their official acts.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1793**:
 
 
• It renewed the **East India Company’s monopoly** over **Indian trade** for an additional period of **twenty years**.
 
• It laid down the rule that the members of the **Board of Control** would be paid out of **Indian revenues**.

questions.question: The Government has proposed to include which Union Territory under the ambit of Article 240 of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandigarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** (MHA) has proposed to amend **Article 240** of the **Constitution of India** to include the **Union Territory** of **Chandigarh** within its ambit.
 
• **Article 240** empowers the **President of India** to make regulations for the peace, progress, and good government of certain **Union Territories**, which have the same force as an **Act of Parliament**.
 
• Currently, **Chandigarh** does not have its own legislative assembly, and most laws are extended from the state of **Punjab** or enacted directly by the **Parliament**.
 
• The proposed inclusion aims to streamline the legislative process, allowing the **President** to enact specific regulations for **Chandigarh** without requiring a formal **Parliamentary** session for every administrative requirement.
 
• This move is intended to enhance **ease of doing business** and simplify the legal framework governing the city's unique administrative structure as a joint capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 240**:

 
 
• Specifically covers **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, **Lakshadweep**, **Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu**, and **Puducherry**.
 
• For **Puducherry**, the **President** can only make regulations when the **Legislative Assembly** is dissolved or suspended.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi**:
 
 
• Governed under **Article 239AA**, which provides a special status with a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers**.
 
• It is not included under **Article 240** because it has its own dedicated constitutional framework for governance.
 
 
 
• **Chandigarh Administration**:
 
 
• It was constituted as a **Union Territory** on **November 1, 1966**, following the reorganization of **Punjab**.
 
• It is managed by an **Administrator** appointed under **Article 239**, traditionally the **Governor of Punjab**.
